Choose how eagerly OpenBehindYou flags nearby faces. Higher sensitivity catches more subtle peekers but can produce more false positives.

When the scene is still, analysis drops to about 1–2 FPS. Motion or a second-face candidate boosts it to about 9–11 FPS for a few seconds, then it settles back down.
A foreground camera service necessarily keeps the camera active. Adaptive frame processing reduces CPU and ML Kit work, but camera use will still be reflected in battery statistics.
ML Kit’s bundled face detector runs locally. Frames are analyzed in memory and discarded immediately.
The manifest removes INTERNET and ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE even if a dependency tries to add them.
Android does not allow a true always-on floating pill without SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW. OpenBehindYou uses a persistent status notification plus a high-priority heads-up alert instead.
Android shows the camera privacy indicator and the ongoing guard notification. Stop Guard at any time from the app or notification.
OpenBehindYou is an open-source, local-only anti-shoulder-surfing guard. Detection is heuristic, not a guarantee of privacy.

Face size, head angle, and proximity heuristics cannot know gaze or intent. A crowded room, reflections, posters, or another person beside you can trigger a warning. Treat alerts as a prompt to check your surroundings, not proof of an attacker. While Guard is on it owns the front camera, so other apps may be unable to use that camera.
